findings.title: The 0.60.0 subprocess-coverage config makes the coverage database unrenderable on this repository: children record their generated fixture files by bare relative path, `coverage json` aborts on the first one, and diff coverage went from 63% measured to `unavailable`
evidence: MEASURED THIS RUN, by the shipped harness: `uv run --group dev verdict-facts --repo . --qa-root .qa` wrote coverage = {"status": "unavailable", "suite_exit_code": 0, "duration_s": 99.09, "reason": "the suite ran but the coverage database could not be rendered: No source for code: 'conftest.py'; see https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/7.16.0/messages.html#error-no-source"}. The suite passed; the measurement did not survive rendering.

REGRESSION, not a standing gap: .qa/state.json at run 5 (commit 32d1c41) records coverage {"status": "measured", "changed_files": 19, "changed_lines": 1125, "changed_lines_executed": 705, "percent": 63}. Same repository, same profile command, one range later, nothing.

PROVEN BY COUNTERFACTUAL, one variable. Both arms ran the profile's own `uv run --group dev python -m coverage run -m pytest tests/ -q -o addopts=` against the real checkout with the harness's own rc file, in temp scratch dirs. Arm A (0.60.0 as shipped, COVERAGE_PROCESS_START pointed at the child rc): suite exit 0, 610 passed in 98.62s, render exit 1, "No source for code: 'conftest.py'", no coverage.json produced. Arm B (identical except COVERAGE_PROCESS_START unset, i.e. 0.59.0 behaviour): suite exit 0, 610 passed in 68.98s, render exit 0, coverage.json produced. The child config is the difference.

MECHANISM, measured: with the child config active over the full suite, `coverage.CoverageData.measured_files()` holds 33 files of which 9 do not exist under the repository root - conftest.py, helper.py, m.py, pkg.py, pricer.py, probe.py, test_m.py, test_pkg.py, test_pricer.py. Every one of the nine carries context 'verdict:subprocess', so every one was written by a child the 0.60.0 config armed. They are the fixture files the suite generates inside pytest tmp_path directories, recorded by bare relative name because src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:634-636 gives the children `relative_files = True` with no `source` and no `include`, and a child's relative paths are relative to the child's own cwd.

src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:642-643 is the trigger: `env = dict(os.environ, COVERAGE_RCFILE=str(rc), COVERAGE_FILE=str(db), COVERAGE_PROCESS_START=str(child_rc))`. coverage 7.16.0 ships the startup hook that acts on it (.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/a1_coverage.pth calls coverage.process_startup when COVERAGE_PROCESS_START is set), so on this machine every Python child of the suite is traced.

The failure is all-or-nothing: `coverage json` aborts the whole render on the first unresolvable path, so one orphan file costs the entire measurement, not one file's worth of it. Confirmed by scope - running only tests/test_issues.py under the same config renders fine (2 measured files, 0 orphans); running the whole suite does not.

NOTHING IN THE SUITE CATCHES IT: 610 tests pass at HEAD. tests/test_diff_coverage.py:265 spawning_repo builds the guarding fixture, and its child is `python -c "import mod; print(mod.b(21))"` with PYTHONPATH pointing back at the repo root - so the only file that child records already exists under the root and no orphan path is ever produced. The docstring calls that fixture 'the shape every CLI test in this repository takes'; the shape this repository's CLI tests actually take is a child that writes and runs source files of its own somewhere else.

SILENT TO THE VALIDATOR TOO: src/verdict_mcp/validate.py:267-280 `_unexercised_diff` refuses a clean `pass` only when `cov.get('status') == 'measured'` and executed == 0. `unavailable` fires nothing, so a gate that stops existing costs a project nothing and says nothing.
SECONDARY COST, measured in the same counterfactual: tracing every child costs 43% of the suite's wall time under coverage (98.62s vs 68.98s), which is paid whether or not the render then succeeds.

root_cause.symptom: diff coverage reports status `unavailable` with reason "No source for code: 'conftest.py'" where run 5 reported 63% of 1125 changed lines executed
root_cause.mechanism: the child rc sets relative_files=True with no source/include, so a child pytest running in a pytest tmp_path records its own generated fixture files under bare relative names; combine merges them into the parent database and `coverage json`, rendering from the repository root, finds no such file and aborts the entire render
root_cause.origin: 7357bfc (v0.60.0, 'the suite's children are the suite'), src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:634-643 - the child config and COVERAGE_PROCESS_START arrived together in this range and nothing else in the range touches coverage rendering
root_cause.class: not a one-site typo: it hits any project whose suite spawns Python children with a different working directory and source files of their own, which is exactly the population VERDICT-F-28 was filed for. Searched the range for other places the harness hands a config to a process it does not control - `_render_cmd` (harness.py:570-579) and `_run_test`'s PYTHONPATH (harness.py:468-471) both target processes rooted at the repo, so this is the only site, but the population it affects is the feature's own target.

findings.title: The outcome ledger still derives `confirmed` from the agent's own `fix_verified` flag, so the published track record records a re-injection the harness never ran - and a decided outcome sticks forever
evidence: LIVE IN THE COMMITTED RECORD AT HEAD. .qa/outcomes.json row for VERDICT-F-20: {"hash": "ebd6bc9f", "id": "VERDICT-F-20", "outcome": "confirmed", "outcome_reason": "fix-verified: the guarding test failed on re-injection", "decided_on": "2026-09-02", "confidence": "proven"}. The same finding's `verification` block in .qa/state.json reads {"test": "t.py::new", "at_previous": "error", "at_head": "error", "summary": "ERROR: file or directory not found: t.py::new -> ERROR: file or directory not found: t.py::new"}. No guarding test failed on re-injection; no test was run at all. The sentence is the harness's, and it is not true.

src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:1026-1028 is the whole rule: `if delta == "RESOLVED" and finding.get("fix_verified") is True: return {"outcome": "confirmed", "outcome_reason": "fix-verified: the guarding test failed on re-injection"}`. Nothing in the branch consults `verification`.

`fix_verified` reaches that branch from either of two sources and the branch cannot tell them apart. Measurement: src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:508-509 sets it when at_previous is `fail` and at_head is `pass`. Claim: src/verdict_mcp/validate.py:483-490 accepts an agent-set `fix_verified` and asks only that the finding carry evidence, and validate.py:91-94 COMPUTED_BY_FINALIZE lists hash, first_seen, age_days, outcome, outcome_reason, carried_forward, verification and resolution_refused - `fix_verified` is deliberately not among them, per agents/verdict.md:665-668.

src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:497-505 only strips the claim when the measurement says `fail` at HEAD. An `error/error` record, or an `unavailable` one, or no record at all, leaves the agent's flag standing and the outcome is minted from it.

PROVEN BY COUNTERFACTUAL against the shipped code at HEAD: `_stamp_outcome({"delta": "RESOLVED", "fix_verified": True, "verification": {"at_previous": "error", "at_head": "error"}})` returns {'outcome': 'confirmed', 'outcome_reason': 'fix-verified: the guarding test failed on re-injection'}. The same call with a pass/pass record - which harness.py:392-395 documents as verifying nothing - returns the identical confirmed outcome.

AND IT STICKS: `_stamp_outcome({"delta": "STILL_OPEN"}, prior={"outcome": "confirmed", ...})` returns confirmed, by the deliberate rule at harness.py:1018-1021. Only a WITHDRAWN overrides it. So a self-graded confirmation cannot be corrected by any later measurement, on any later run, forever.

WHAT MAKES IT MATTER: this is the input to the published number. src/verdict_mcp/state.py:317-323 buckets exactly this `outcome` by confidence, and harness.py:1632-1651 renders it as Track record. .qa/state.json calibration currently reads by_confidence.proven {"confirmed": 10, "refuted": 0, "decided": 10} - at least one of those ten is a claim the harness contradicted in the same file.

CONTRADICTS ITS OWN DOCUMENTATION: docs/state-schema.md:98 says `findings[].outcome` is 'computed ... written by verdict-finalize, never by the agent. Confirmed = regressed, or resolved-and-fix-verified.' agents/verdict.md:661-663 says 'You never set the outcome. outcome and outcome_reason are computed from what happened. Marking your own work correct is the one thing a tester must never be able to do.' On the resolved path the agent's boolean is the sole input.

DISTINCT FROM VERDICT-F-30, which is resolved this run. F-30 was filed against the report renderer (harness.py:1616-1623) and its root_cause class link says 'This is the single site'; the search that produced that line swept renderers and did not reach the outcome derivation. The 0.57.0 fix changed only render_report, and it works: on the very same finding the report now prints 'Fix verification: 0 verified' and names it under 'claims fix_verified the measurement does not show'. The report is honest and the ledger beneath it is not.

root_cause.symptom: outcomes.json publishes `confirmed` with the reason 'fix-verified: the guarding test failed on re-injection' for a finding whose only measurement errored at both commits
root_cause.mechanism: _stamp_outcome reads the boolean `fix_verified` and never the `verification` record beside it, and `fix_verified` is writable by the judgment as well as by the measurement, so the two sources are indistinguishable at the point the outcome is minted
root_cause.origin: the branch predates this range and was not touched by it (`git log --oneline 32d1c41..HEAD -- src/verdict_mcp/state.py` is empty; harness.py:1026 is unchanged in the range). What is new is that 0.57.0 fixed the visible half and left this one, which is why it now reads as a discrepancy between the report and the ledger rather than as one consistent error
root_cause.class: searched every consumer of fix_verified in src/: render_report (harness.py:1712-1728, fixed in 0.57.0), _apply_verification (harness.py:497-509, the measurement's own writer), _stamp_outcome (harness.py:1026, this site) and a comment in issues.py:16. This is the remaining site, and it is the one that feeds the number the contract says the model must not be able to influence.

findings.title: Fix verification still copies back only the cited test's own file, so a regression test that lands with a new fixture or helper in the same commit errors at the previous commit and is silently never verified
evidence: PROVEN BY COUNTERFACTUAL in a scratch two-commit git repository (tempfile dir, never the checkout), driving the shipped collect() and merge() at HEAD. Commit A: buggy pkg.py, a conftest.py with no fixtures, a test file. Commit B: pkg.py fixed, a new `qty` fixture added to conftest.py, and the regression test `test_pending(qty)` appended to the existing test file. Verification record: {"test": "test_pkg.py::test_pending", "at_previous": "error", "at_head": "pass", "summary": "1 error in 0.00s -> 1 passed in 0.00s"}. merge() returned fix_verified None, outcome 'unknown', reason 'resolved but not fix-verified - absence is not proof'.

src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:455-462 is the scope: `test_file = test_id.split("::", 1)[0]; src, dst = Path(repo) / test_file, scratch / test_file; if src.is_file(): ... shutil.copyfile(src, dst)`. Exactly one file travels back to the old commit - the one the node id names. A fixture, a helper module, a shared factory or a conftest the new test depends on stays at its old commit version, and the test cannot even be collected.

The VERDICT-F-25 fix this replaces is genuinely good and is resolved this run: with the same probe shape but the dependency living inside the test file itself, at_previous now reads `fail` and fix_verified is set. The remaining gap is one level out - the test's dependencies, not the test.

FAILS SILENT, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL COST: `error` is neither `fail` nor `pass`, so harness.py:497-509 takes neither the refusal branch nor the fix_verified branch, and verification_notes says nothing about a counterfactual that could not be constructed. The finding resolves with no verification and no explanation, and outcomes.json takes it as undecided - which depresses the very precision rate the feature exists to make publishable.

THIS REPOSITORY IS THE POPULATION: tests/conftest.py exists precisely so fixtures are shared across test files, and tests/test_verification.py:20 does `from conftest import judgment`. A regression test added here alongside a new conftest fixture is the ordinary case, not a corner.

VERDICT-F-25's own root_cause class link reads 'searched the verification path for other file-vs-symbol granularity assumptions ... so this is the only site.' The search was over the copy-back itself and did not consider what the copied test imports. That is the incompleteness this finding records.

root_cause.symptom: a genuinely fixed defect whose regression test needs a fixture added in the same commit reports at_previous 'error' and never earns fix_verified
root_cause.mechanism: the counterfactual copies a single file by node-id prefix, while the object that must travel back to the old commit is the test's transitive dependency closure - conftest, helpers, factories
root_cause.origin: the copy-back's file scope is original to the feature (v0.53.0) and survived the VERDICT-F-25 fix in 6d593d4, which corrected the CONDITION (copy only when absent) without widening the SCOPE (one file)
root_cause.class: HYPOTHESIS on remedy, not on the defect: copying the whole tests/ tree from HEAD would close it, but might mask a genuine collection failure at the old commit, and I did not test that. What is proven is the gap, not the right fix.

findings.title: The recurrence-filing window is exactly one run wide: a REGRESSED finding that verdict-issues does not see on the run whose delta says REGRESSED can never be re-filed, and the operator is told it is already filed
evidence: PROVEN by probe against the shipped CLI at HEAD, using the repository's own gh stub and helpers (tests/test_issues.py make_home/run/calls, VERDICT_HOME in a tempdir). Run 7: one open Critical, `--create` files issue #1. Run 8: same id, delta REGRESSED - and verdict-issues is simply not invoked on that run. Run 9: same id, delta STILL_OPEN, `--create` invoked. Output: 'verdict-issues: created 0 (0 recurrence), 1 already filed, 0 deferred by --limit'. gh calls: 1. Ledger `previous` trail: None. The recurrence was never filed and never can be.

src/verdict_mcp/issues.py:107-113 is the rule: `elif f.get("delta") == "REGRESSED" and prior.get("run_number") != run: action = "refile"`. The discriminator is `delta`, which describes only the transition at the run that observed it; by the next run the same finding is STILL_OPEN and the branch cannot fire again.

The consequence is the sentence VERDICT-F-27 was filed about, one run later: '1 already filed' asserts the tracker is current, while the issue it refers to was in all likelihood closed by whoever fixed the finding the first time. Same wrong claim, narrower window.

The durable discriminator is already in the ledger and still unread on this path: issues.py:225-226 writes `"hash": f.get("hash")` on every entry, and a recurrence after a resolution changes the hash. A comparison against the stored hash, or against a `resolved_at` marker, would not depend on catching the one run where delta was REGRESSED.

SCOPE, stated honestly: the nightly loop documented in docs/nightly.md runs verdict-issues every run, so the window is usually met and the 0.59.0 fix works in the intended flow - which is why this is Minor and P3, not a repeat of VERDICT-F-27's severity. It bites the ad-hoc operator and the run that failed or was skipped.

VERDICT-F-27 is resolved this run and its guard is real: re-injecting the old `action = "exists" if fid in ledger else "create"` into a scratch copy makes tests/test_issues.py::test_a_finding_that_came_back_is_filed_again fail. This finding is the residual, not a retraction of that.

root_cause.symptom: a finding that came back is reported as 'already filed' whenever verdict-issues is not run on the exact run that observed the regression
root_cause.mechanism: the refile guard keys on `delta`, a per-run transition marker, rather than on a durable difference between the filed occurrence and the current one
root_cause.class: searched issues.py for other per-run values used as durable state: `run_number` is stored and compared, which is durable and correct; `delta` is the only transient one load-bearing in a decision. Single site.

findings.title: The VERDICT_STRICT bash guard reads '>' and '<' inside quoted strings and heredoc bodies as output redirection and resolves the phantom target against the checkout, blocking read-only QA commands
evidence: UNTOUCHED IN THIS RANGE: `git log --oneline 32d1c41..HEAD -- hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py` is empty. The mechanism is unchanged since it was filed.

RE-PROVEN THREE MORE TIMES THIS SESSION, on three read-only commands, with the checkout unmodified throughout. (1) `rm -rf $SC` where $SC was a shell variable holding a scratchpad path - refused with "rm targets '$SC (unresolved $variable - use a literal path)'". That one is arguably correct behaviour and is recorded as the guard's honest half. (2) A `<<'PY'` heredoc whose Python body contained the f-string `f"          -> {test...}"` - refused with "output redirection targets '<checkout>/{test.split('::')[-1]}:'". (3) `git log --format=fuller`-adjacent: `git log --format='%H%n%an <%ae>%n...'` - refused with "output redirection targets '<checkout>/%n%(trailers)%n---''", from a `<` inside a single-quoted argument.

NEW INFORMATION FROM CASE (3): the previous reproductions were all about '>'. This one is '<', inside single quotes, in a git format string - so the scan treats both redirection operators the same way and quoting is invisible to it in both directions. Case (2) confirms run 5's finding that heredoc framing is also invisible.

The blocked constructs are ordinary in the material a tester must read: '->' is a Python return annotation appearing on 100+ lines of this repository's own source, and '<...>' is the shape of every email address in a git author field.

COST, measured: three retries this session, each costing one round trip and a reworded command. No finding was lost - I reformulated each command and got the evidence - which is why this stays Minor. It would rise to Major if a project's only route to a piece of evidence went through a blocked shape.

findings.title: Fix verification copies the cited test back to the old commit only when the whole test FILE is absent there, so a regression test appended to an existing test file yields at_previous 'error' and fix_verified is silently never set
evidence: FIXED at src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:455-462 in 6d593d4 (v0.57.0): the conditional is now `if src.is_file():` with `differs = (not dst.exists()) or dst.read_bytes() != src.read_bytes()`, so the cited test's file always comes from HEAD and `test_copied_from_head` keeps its meaning.

FIX-VERIFIED BY RE-INJECTION, which is what run 5's next-run focus asked for. In a scratch copy of HEAD (git archive into a temp dir, never the checkout) the pre-fix form `if not dst.exists() and src.is_file():` was restored and the guard re-run: tests/test_verification.py::test_a_regression_test_appended_to_an_existing_file_verifies went red - '1 failed in 0.46s'. Restoring the fix returns it to green. The guard is real, not decorative.

AND THE APPENDED CASE ITSELF WAS RE-RUN, not just its guard. The shipped test builds exactly the two-commit repository run 5 specified - commit A has test_pkg.py containing only test_other, commit B fixes pkg.py and APPENDS test_pending to the same file - and asserts rec['test_copied_from_head'] is True, (at_previous, at_head) == ('fail', 'pass'), and merge() setting fix_verified True. It passes at HEAD. at_previous reads `fail`, not `error`.

The paired negative case is guarded too: tests/test_verification.py::test_a_test_file_the_fix_did_not_touch_is_not_reported_as_copied asserts test_copied_from_head is absent when the file is identical at both commits, so the flag did not become noise.

RESIDUAL, filed separately as VERDICT-F-33 rather than held against this finding: the copy-back is still one file wide, so a regression test that needs a fixture added in the same commit still errors at the previous commit.
